html:
From about 1850 to 1930 some 1.3 million Swedes emigrated to the United States, around a fifth of the population. Most sailed from Gothenburg.

Rapid population growth, small farms and the famine years of 1867 to 1869 drove them, as did the pull of cheap land in the Midwest. Religious dissenters and young people seeking work joined them. Minnesota, Illinois and Chicago gained large Swedish communities.

Sweden worried about losing so many people and held an inquiry into emigration from 1907. Industrial growth at home slowed the flow. Vilhelm Moberg's novels The Emigrants told the story to later generations. Compare the Norwegian and Irish emigrations. See Sweden.
